papers.title_zh: IB-IIIB期肺腺癌术后EGFR突变检测率仅56%，医院间与患者间差异显著
papers.title_en: Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor-Mutation Testing in Patients with Resected Stage IB-IIIB Lung Adenocarcinoma: Are Guidelines Followed?
papers.authors: Pohlman A, Seder CW, Woodard GA, Coughlin JM, Odeh B, Abdelsattar ZM
papers.affiliation_highlight: Stritch School of Medicine, Loyola University Chicago, Maywood, IL; Department of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery, L…
papers.results: 25,124例患者中14,061例（56.0%）接受EGFR突变检测；医院间检测率差异显著（最低五分位20.8% vs 最高五分位89.7%，p<0.001）；学术中心更可能开展检测（40.2% vs 38.6%，p=0.009），都市地区医院（84.2% vs 81.8%，p<0.001）；患者层面女性（aOR 1.13，p<0.001）、亚裔（aOR 1.45，p<0001）、从不吸烟者（aOR 1.22，p<0.001）更可能被检测
papers.authors_conclusion: 接受手术的IB-IIIB期肺腺癌患者中仅1/2接受EGFR突变检测，医院与患者之间诊疗差异大；需要进一步的质量改进举措针对医院和医务人员，提高意识以确保指南一致性诊疗
papers.ai_note: 摘要未报告任何OR的95%CI，仅给点估计与P值，效应量精度信息不足；学术中心40.2% vs 38.6%的绝对差仅1.6个百分点却以p=0.009强调，大样本下统计学显著与临床意义可能不匹配；总检测率56.0%的分母是否含检测结果缺失/记录不全的患者信息不足；未按分期、年龄或驱动基因后续治疗（如奥希替尼辅助治疗资格）分层，检测率缺口对辅助治疗决策的实际影响无法评估；结论中'质量改进举措'属规范性推断，超出本观察性描述设计所能证明的范围

pico.p: 2021-2023年NCDB中接受手术的IB-IIIB期肺腺癌患者25,124例，来自906家医院
pico.ic: 无干预；比较不同医院（按风险与可靠性调整后检测率五分位）及不同患者人口学/社会经济特征组间的EGFR检测率

papers.reason: 反映可切除肺腺癌术后EGFR检测指南依从性缺口及其医院/人群不均衡，直接影响术后辅助靶向治疗（奥希替尼）患者筛选与转诊质量改进，并为胸外科中心检测流程审计提供全国基线
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Testing for Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR)-mutations in resected stage IB-IIIB non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer is now standard for all patients, regardless of demographics. Current hospital- and patient-level testing rates and trends are unknown. In this context, we analyze hospital- and patient-level variation in EGFR testing nationally. METHODS: We used the national cancer database (NCDB) to identify patients with stage IB-IIIB lung adenocarcinoma between 2021-2023 undergoing resection. We used a hierarchical multivariable logistic regression model to create risk- and reliability-adjusted EGFR testing rates across hospitals and compare those across quintiles. We also used a logistic regression model to compare the likelihood of testing based on patient demographics and socioeconomic factors. RESULTS: Of 25,124 stage IB-IIIB patients with lung adenocarcinoma undergoing surgery, 14,061 (56.0%) patients at 906 hospitals were tested for EGFR mutations. There was significant variation in testing rates between hospitals (20.8% lowest quintile vs 89.7% highest, p<0.001). Hospitals were more likely to perform EGFR testing if they were academic centers (40.2% vs 38.6%, p=0.009) and reside in a metropolitan area (84.2% vs 81.8%, p<0.001). Patients were more likely to be tested if they were female (aOR 1.13, p<0.001), Asian (aOR 1.45, p<0.001), and never smokers (aOR 1.22, p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Only 1 in 2 patients with stage IB-IIIB lung adenocarcinoma treated surgically are tested for EGFR mutations, with wide variation in care between hospitals and patients. Further quality initiatives are needed to target hospitals and providers and raise awareness to ensure guideline-concordant care.

papers.authors: Weber M, Gimeno-Santos E, Wuyts M, Herrero-Cortina B, Troosters T, Puhan MA
papers.affiliation_highlight: Epidemiology, Biostatistics and Prevention Institute, University of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland.
papers.results: 再住院：OR 0.52，95%CI 0.32至0.84，I²=69%，中等确定性；全因死亡率：OR 0.84，95%CI 0.49至1.43，I²=33%，低确定性；HRQL（SGRQ总分）：MD -9.05，95%CI -12.60至-5.50，I²=70%，高确定性，超过4分MID；SGRQ活动与影响域超过MID，症状域无差异；6MWD：MD 57.79 m，95%CI 41.68至73.91，I²=89%，高确定性；Egger检验：再住院P=0.02、死亡率P=0.02、SGRQ P=0.45、6MWT P=0.12

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Guidelines have provided positive recommendations for pulmonary rehabilitation after severe exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), but results are heterogeneous and new randomised controlled trials (RCTs) continue to be published. OBJECTIVES: To assess the effects of pulmonary rehabilitation after COPD exacerbations on hospital admissions (critical outcome) and other important and patient-centred outcomes (mortality, health-related quality of life (HRQL) and exercise capacity). SEARCH METHODS: We identified studies through searches of the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE ALL, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov and the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (WHO ICTRP). Searches were current to 2 June 2026. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: RCTs comparing pulmonary rehabilitation of any duration (at least exercise training but no minimum number of exercise sessions) after exacerbation of COPD versus usual care were eligible. Usual care groups received conventional community care without rehabilitation. OUTCOMES: The four main outcomes were hospital readmissions, mortality, HRQL and exercise capacity. RISK OF BIAS: We assessed the risk of bias in the included RCTs as high, low or unclear, using the Cochrane RoB 1 tool. SYNTHESIS METHODS: We expected substantial heterogeneity across trials due to the diversity of rehabilitation programmes (i.e. number of completed exercise sessions; type, intensity and supervision of exercise training; and patient education), duration of follow-up (under three months versus three months or longer) and risk of bias (random sequence generation, allocation concealment and blinding). Therefore, we conducted prespecified subgroup analyses. We used random-effects models and standard Cochrane methods for this update, and assessed the certainty of evidence using GRADE. INCLUDED STUDIES: For this update, we added 20 studies and included a total of 40 studies (2825 participants). SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Rehabilitation programmes showed great diversity in terms of exercise training (number of completed exercise sessions; type, intensity and supervision), patient education (from none to extensive self-management programmes) and how they were organised (within one setting, e.g. pulmonary rehabilitation, to across several settings, e.g. hospital, outpatient centre and home). In 12 studies, participants completed extensive pulmonary rehabilitation, and in 25 studies, participants completed pulmonary rehabilitation ranging from not extensive to moderately extensive. We could not determine how extensive the programmes were in three studies, owing to missing information. Thirteen studies (1229 participants) contributed data on hospital readmissions, with follow-up ranging from three months to 18 months. Moderate-certainty evidence indicates that pulmonary rehabilitation after an exacerbation likely reduces the risk of hospital readmission when compared with usual care (pooled odds ratio (OR) 0.52, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.32 to 0.84; I2 = 69%). Twenty-two studies (1677 participants) contributed data on all-cause mortality, but only 11 trials (1196 participants) were included in the pooled effect estimate because the remaining studies reported no deaths in either group. Follow-up in these studies ranged from the duration of the hospital stay to 48 months. Low-certainty evidence suggests that pulmonary rehabilitation after an exacerbation may reduce all-cause mortality slightly when compared with usual care (pooled OR 0.84, 95% CI 0.49 to 1.43; I2 = 33%). Twelve studies (1118 participants) used the St George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) to assess HRQL, with follow-up ranging from the duration of the hospital stay to 12 months. High-certainty evidence indicates that, when compared with usual care, pulmonary rehabilitation after an exacerbation results in a large improvement in HRQL, as measured by the SGRQ total score (mean difference (MD) -9.05, 95% CI -12.60 to -5.50; I2 = 70%), exceeding the minimal important difference (MID) of four points. There was evidence of a difference between pulmonary rehabilitation and usual care for the SGRQ activity and impacts domains (effects exceeding the MID), but no evidence of a difference for the symptoms domain. Twenty-two studies (1464 participants) used the six-minute walk distance (6MWD) to assess exercise capacity, with follow-up ranging from four days to 208 weeks. High-certainty evidence indicates that pulmonary rehabilitation after an exacerbation results in a large improvement in 6MWD when compared with usual care (MD 57.79 m, 95% CI 41.68 to 73.91; I2 = 89%). Heterogeneity appeared to be driven mainly by differences between studies showing very large effects and those showing smaller effects but still evidence of between-group differences. The overall results of this review have not changed to an important extent compared with results reported in the previous version of this review. Overall, the risk of bias was judged to be low or unclear across most domains. However, the lack of participant blinding raised concerns for subjectively reported outcomes (HRQL). High risks of selection bias and attrition bias were identified in a small number of studies, while a larger proportion of studies were at high risk for reporting bias. Egger's test indicated evidence of funnel plot asymmetry for hospital readmission (P = 0.02) and mortality (P = 0.02), but not for SGRQ (P = 0.45) or the six-minute walk test (P = 0.12). Visual inspection suggested that the asymmetry was more consistent with small-study effects than with clear evidence of missing negative studies. AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Moderate-certainty evidence indicates that pulmonary rehabilitation likely reduces hospital readmissions, while evidence for mortality is of low certainty. However, some recent studies showed no benefit of rehabilitation on hospital readmissions and mortality. Such heterogeneity of effects on hospital readmissions and mortality may be explained to some extent by the extensiveness of rehabilitation programmes and by the methodological quality of the included studies. High-certainty evidence shows moderate to large effects of pulmonary rehabilitation on HRQL and exercise capacity in people with COPD after an exacerbation. While additional RCTs comparing rehabilitation to no rehabilitation seem questionable scientifically and ethically, future research must investigate how rehabilitation programmes can be designed and implemented to be feasible, cost-effective and attractive and accessible for patients and healthcare providers in the long term. Research must also investigate how the organisation of such programmes within specific healthcare systems determines their effects after COPD exacerbations on hospital readmissions and mortality. FUNDING: This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding. REGISTRATION: Protocol (2005) DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD005305 Original review (2009) DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD005305.pub2 Review update (2011) DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD005305.pub3 Review update (2016) DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD005305.pub4.

papers.authors: Sakowitz S, Bakhtiyar SS, Sanaiha Y, Mehta D, Shemin RJ, Benharash P
papers.affiliation_highlight: Cardiovascular Outcomes Research Laboratories (CORELAB), University of California, Los Angeles, CA.
papers.results: EVLP供肺比例由2018年5%升至2024年10%、2025年8%（P trend <0.001）。LAS时代：HVC中2年结局相似，non-HVC结局较差（摘要未给出具体数值）。CAS时代模拟RCT中：non-HVC受者EVLP与2年患者死亡风险升高相关（HR: 2.43, CI: 1.36-4.34, P=0.003），与2年移植物失功风险升高相关（HR: 2.52, CI: 1.31-4.84, P=0.005）；HVC中EVLP与结局相似（摘要未给出HR/CI/P）。

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Ex vivo lung perfusion (EVLP) has been championed as a disruptive strategy to expand the lung transplantation (LT) donor pool, yet contemporary evidence remains limited. Using a real-world cohort, we emulated a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to characterize the causal effect of EVLP on post-LT survival. METHODS: LT recipients ≥18 years were identified from the 2018-2025 Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network. Annual hospital LT volume was computed; centers in the top quartile (>54 LT/y) were designated high-volume centers (HVCs). Using target trial emulation with clone-censor-weight methodology, we simulated a pragmatic, open-label RCT comparing EVLP with standard allografts at HVCs and non-HVCs. Survival was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox models. RESULTS: Among 20,627 LTs, 1419 (7%) received EVLP allografts. The proportion of EVLP allografts increased across all centers, from 5% in 2018 to 10% in 2024 and 8% in 2025 (P trend <0.001). In the Lung Allocation Score era, LT using EVLP allografts yielded similar 2-year outcomes at HVC, but inferior outcomes at non-HVC. In the Composite Allocation Score period, however, EVLP was associated with significantly worse survival at non-HVC. In the emulated RCT among CAS-era recipients, EVLP remained independently associated with similar outcomes at HVC, but increased 2-year hazards of patient mortality (HR: 2.43, CI: 1.36-4.34, P=0.003) and allograft failure at non-HVC (HR: 2.52, CI: 1.31-4.84, P=0.005). CONCLUSIONS: EVLP was associated with comparable survival at HVC but inferior outcomes at non-HVC. These findings highlight the critical role of hospital context and center experience in determining the effectiveness and safety of EVLP and call for standardization of protocols across centers.

papers.title_en: Comparison of Additional Surgical Resection Versus Surveillance Only in Patients with Early Esophageal Cancer After Non-curative Endoscopic Resection: A Meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Zhou Y, Qi B, Cao J, Cao X, Zhang S, Xu L, Cheng Y, Lin Z et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Gastrointestinal Surgery, Affiliated Hospital of North Sichuan Medical College, Nanchong, Sichuan Province…
papers.results: 7项研究493例。5年总生存（risk ratio 1.40; 95%CI 1.24-1.58）、5年无复发生存（risk ratio 1.34; 95%CI 1.08-1.67）均显著优于随访；癌症特异性生存合并HR 4.64（95%CI 1.09-19.76）亦偏向手术。相比之下，3年各终点及总生存、无复发生存的时间事件HR均未达统计学显著。
papers.authors_conclusion: Additional surgery offers significant long-term survival benefits for eligible patients with early-stage esophageal cancer. Clinical decision-making should be individualized, and future high-quality studies are needed to further validate its efficacy across diverse populations.
papers.ai_note: 全部为非随机观察性研究合并，追加手术组与随访组存在明确选择偏倚（体能状态好、可耐受手术者更可能入手术组），不能等同于RCT证据。3年终点与OS/RFS时间事件HR均为阴性，仅5年OS/RFS阳性，作者结论聚焦'长期获益'，存在终点选择性强调的可能，且未说明3年与5年结果不一致的原因。CSS的HR 4.64方向与常规HR编码（>1表示风险更高）相反，提示可能为随访/手术反向编码，且95%CI 1.09-19.76极宽，估计极不稳定。摘要未给出异质性指标（I²）及随机/固定效应模型的选择依据。检索截止日期标注为2026年9月29日，需核对。样本量小（493例、7项研究）。

pico.p: 早期食管癌内镜切除后非治愈性切除（存在高危病理特征）患者，7项研究共493例
pico.ic: 追加手术 vs 仅随访监测（surveillance only）

papers.reason: 直接影响非治愈性内镜切除后是否追加手术的临床决策与多学科讨论；同时提示现有证据全部来自观察性研究，为后续前瞻性研究设计与患者筛选标准提供参考基线。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Esophageal cancer is a highly lethal malignant tumor of the digestive system. Patients with early esophageal cancer often undergo endoscopic resection, but postoperative non-curative resection is frequently undertaken because of the presence of high-risk pathological features. Controversy over subsequent management strategies remains. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane databases through September 29, 2026, yielded seven studies involving 493 patients. A meta-analysis was performed using random-effects or fixed-effects models, and study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and the Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions-I tool. RESULTS: This meta-analysis included seven studies. Compared with surveillance, additional surgery was associated with significantly improved 5-year survival: 5-year overall survival (risk ratio 1.40; 95% confidence [CI] 1.24-1.58), and 5-year recurrence-free survival (risk ratio 1.34; 95% CI 1.08-1.67), all favoring surgery. The pooled hazard ratio for cancer-specific survival also favored surgery (4.64; 95% CI 1.09-19.76). By contrast, the 3-year endpoints and the time-to-event hazard ratios for overall and recurrence-free survival did not reach statistical significance. CONCLUSION: Additional surgery offers significant long-term survival benefits for eligible patients with early-stage esophageal cancer. Clinical decision-making should be individualized, and future high-quality studies are needed to further validate its efficacy across diverse populations.

papers.title_zh: 定量CT将CPFE划分为纤维化主导与肺气肿主导表型，纤维化主导者调整后全因死亡风险更高（HR 1.36）
papers.title_en: Quantitative CT Phenotypes and Prognosis in Combined Pulmonary Fibrosis and Emphysema.
papers.authors: Wang H, Ni Y, Deng Y, Huang S, Qiang Y, Yang X, Liu A, Wang J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical College, Beijing, China.
papers.results: 中位随访2.59年内513例死亡；调整后纤维化主导表型全因死亡风险升高（HR 1.36, 95%CI 1.13-1.62, P<.001）。纤维化主导组纤维化百分比中位18% vs 肺气肿主导组10%（P<.001）；肺气肿主导组肺气肿百分比中位7% vs 纤维化主导组6%（P<.001）。摘要报告C指数与校准用于评估模型性能，但未给出具体数值
papers.authors_conclusion: Quantitative CT helped identify emphysema- and fibrosis-dominant CPFE phenotypes with different prognoses. The fibrosis-dominant phenotype was associated with higher all-cause mortality.
papers.ai_note: 表型切点为数据驱动的简单二分（纤维化%≥肺气肿%），非预设或外部验证阈值，存在人群限定松动风险；两组定量指标差异本身即由该定义决定（纤维化主导组纤维化更高、肺气肿主导组肺气肿更高），属循环论证式的组间比较，非独立发现。摘要称使用C指数与校准评估模型性能但未报告数值、未说明调整变量清单，信息不足；系二次分析、单一定量算法、无外部验证；未区分纤维化相关与肺气肿相关死因，全因死亡终点可能稀释表型特异性差异。

pico.p: CPFE患者1583例（中位年龄65岁[IQR 58-71]；男性1186例），2017年1月至2024年12月入组，中位随访2.59年，期间513例死亡
pico.ic: 纤维化主导表型（纤维化百分比≥肺气肿百分比）823例（52%） vs 肺气肿主导表型760例（48%）；均为AI工作站自动分割定量HRCT后的表型分组，无干预

papers.reason: 为CPFE患者预后分层与随访强度决策提供AI定量CT依据，并为基于影像组学/定量参数的呼吸慢病预后队列设计提供对照基线与效应量参考。
papers.abstract_en: Background Combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema (CPFE) has heterogeneous outcomes, and visual assessment or separate measurement of emphysema and fibrosis does not directly identify which structural component predominates in an individual patient. Purpose To determine whether quantitative CT enables objective stratification of CPFE into fibrosis-dominant and emphysema-dominant phenotypes and to evaluate their distinct clinical trajectories and prognostic implications. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis of a prospective multicenter observational study included patients with CPFE enrolled between January 2017 and December 2024. A fixed commercial artificial intelligence workstation automatically segmented the lungs and quantified emphysema and fibrosis on high-resolution CT scans. Participants were classified as having the fibrosis-dominant phenotype when the fibrosis percentage was equal to or greater than the emphysema percentage, and as having the emphysema-dominant phenotype otherwise. Group comparisons used the t test, Wilcoxon rank-sum test, χ2 test, or Fisher exact test. Cox models were used to assess all-cause mortality; C index and calibration were used to assess model performance. Results The study population included 1583 participants (median age, 65 years [IQR, 58-71 years]; 1186 men); 823 (52%) had the fibrosis-dominant phenotype, and 760 (48%) had the emphysema-dominant phenotype. The fibrosis-dominant group had a higher fibrosis percentage than the emphysema-dominant group (median, 18% vs 10%; P < .001), whereas the emphysema-dominant group had a higher emphysema percentage (median, 7% vs 6%; P < .001). During a median follow-up of 2.59 years, 513 deaths occurred. The fibrosis-dominant phenotype was associated with higher mortality after adjustment (hazard ratio, 1.36 [95% CI: 1.13, 1.62]; P < .001). Conclusion Quantitative CT helped identify emphysema- and fibrosis-dominant CPFE phenotypes with different prognoses. The fibrosis-dominant phenotype was associated with higher all-cause mortality. Clinical trial registration no. NCT04370158 © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Grenier in this issue.

papers.authors: Gilley KN, Garness J, Khan A, Materia BR, Carpenter B, Shabrang M, Beckabir W, Woodcock MG et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Bowles Center for Alcohol Studies, School of Medicine, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Chapel Hill, NC 2759…
papers.results: 在两种小鼠模型中，中-重度乙醇摄入方案使ICI疗效降低约50%并增加肿瘤复发；在肺癌患者中，规律饮酒与ICI生存获益减少相关（摘要未给出具体HR/CI/P数值）；膀胱癌、黑色素瘤和头颈癌患者中结果不明确（饮酒报告过于有限）。小鼠MB49膀胱瘤模型：乙醇摄入减少肿瘤浸润T细胞数量，肿瘤相关CD4+ T细胞中TH17相对TH1极化偏移，减少组织驻留记忆T细胞比例，增加表达TIGIT的T细胞比例，并诱导肿瘤相关T细胞中SREBP介导的脂质信号；以抗体阻断TIGIT、或在较低程度上以betulin抑制SREBP信号，可改善PD1受体阻断疗效

Future incorporation of patients' alcohol use in cancer databases will help define its effect on the outcome of various therapies in multiple cancers.
papers.ai_note: 信息不足：患者队列为回顾性设计，摘要未报告样本量、饮酒定义与量化、生存分析的具体效应量（HR/CI/P）及混杂因素校正情况；患者数据仅为关联性描述，主要机制证据来自小鼠模型，且'疗效降低约50%'为小鼠实验结果，不能直接外推至人群；肺癌以外癌种因饮酒报告受限而结果不明确，存在选择性报告与人群限定松动风险；次要探索性指标（TIGIT、SREBP、TH17/TH1）机制链条较丰富，但缺乏人群层面验证

pico.ic: 小鼠：中-重度乙醇摄入 vs 对照，联合PD1阻断（±抗TIGIT抗体或betulin）；患者：规律饮酒 vs 不饮酒/饮酒状态分组的ICI疗效比较

papers.reason: 提示饮酒这一可干预的生活方式因素可能削弱晚期NSCLC等ICI疗效，并提出TIGIT共靶向的联合策略，为ICI疗效差异的混杂因素分析与联合治疗假说提供依据；同时其人群证据薄弱，可作为评估伴随行为因素研究设计的参照
papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) has improved outcomes for some patients with advanced malignancies, but relatively few have a complete response. Alcohol use is common and impairs adaptive immunity. Here, we explored the link between alcohol use and ICI efficacy in mouse models of lung and bladder cancers and performed a retrospective assessment of a cohort of patients with cancer receiving ICI therapy. In both mouse models, a regimen of moderate-to-heavy ethanol intake reduced ICI efficacy by ∼50% and increased tumor recurrence. In patients with lung cancer, regular alcohol use was associated with reduced survival benefit from ICI. Effects were less definitive in patients with bladder cancer, melanoma, and head and neck cancer, in whom alcohol use reporting was too limited. In mice bearing MB49 bladder tumors, ethanol intake reduced the number of tumor-infiltrated T cells favoring T helper 17 cell (TH17 cell) over TH1 cell phenotypes in tumor-associated CD4+ T cells. It also reduced the number of tissue-resident memory T cells, increased the proportion of T cells expressing the alternative immune checkpoint receptor TIGIT, and induced SREBP-mediated lipid signaling in tumor-associated T cells. Blocking TIGIT with antibodies or, to a lesser extent, inhibiting SREBP signaling with betulin improved the efficacy of PD1 receptor blockade. The findings suggest that regular alcohol use negatively affects ICI efficacy, which may be counteracted by cotargeting TIGIT. Future incorporation of patients' alcohol use in cancer databases will help define its effect on the outcome of various therapies in multiple cancers.

papers.title_en: Independent Validation of the LIONS PREY in Patients Undergoing Navigational Bronchoscopy.
papers.authors: Büscher E, Funke F, Darwiche K, Karpf-Wissel R, Taube C, Bölükbas S, Webendörfer M, Schuler M et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Interventional Pneumology, Department of Pulmonary Medicine, University Hospital Essen-Ruhrlandklinik, Essen…
papers.results: 193个可评估病灶中134个（69.4%）组织学确诊恶性。恶性病灶生长动态更高（2.7 ± 4.1 mm vs. 1.0 ± 4.3 mm，p < 0.001），毛刺征比例更高（56.0% vs. 23.7%，p < 0.001）。LIONS PREY的ROC曲线下面积（AUC）为0.94，优于Herder（AUC 0.72；p < 0.001）和Brock（AUC 0.62；p < 0.001）。正确分类率LIONS PREY最高（85.0%）vs. Herder（70.3%）和Brock（69.1%）（均p < 0.001）。
papers.authors_conclusion: The LIONS PREY demonstrated superior predictive accuracy over Brock and Herder in high-risk patients undergoing navigational bronchoscopy, supporting its clinical utility for malignancy risk stratification.
papers.ai_note: 方法学疑点：①题为“independent validation”但为单中心回顾性验证，LIONS PREY原始推导人群若与本高危支气管镜队列高度重叠，AUC 0.94可能存在人群/谱系重叠导致的乐观偏倚，摘要未说明推导集来源；②仅报告判别力（AUC、分类准确率），未报告校准度（校准曲线/Hosmer-Lemeshow），无法判断风险预测是否校准良好；③队列恶性率高达69.4%，属高选择性支气管镜人群，分类准确率依赖该患病率与阈值，向肺癌筛查低患病率人群外推存疑；④未报告各模型所用阈值及决策曲线/净获益分析；⑤分类准确率与AUC比较均仅以p值呈现，未给出AUC差值的95%CI。

pico.p: 2019年12月至2024年3月于三级学术中心首次接受导航支气管镜评估外周肺结节的患者，193个可评估病灶，其中134个（69.4%）组织学确诊恶性
pico.ic: 干预：LIONS PREY模型；对照：Brock模型与Herder模型（同一队列内三模型判别力与分类准确率比较）

papers.reason: 影响外周肺结节行导航支气管镜前的风险分层工具选择——在高危支气管镜人群中提供LIONS PREY相对Brock/Herder的判别力对照数据，可为结节恶性概率评估与是否进一步侵入性检查的决策提供依据；同时其单中心回顾性、仅报告判别力的局限为后续多中心校准验证研究设计提供参照。
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Accurate malignancy risk prediction of pulmonary lesions is essential in the context of lung cancer screening and early diagnosis. Widely used risk prediction tools, such as the Brock and Herder models, have shown limited performance in high-risk cohorts referred for bronchoscopic evaluation. The LIONS PREY (lung lesion score predicts malignancy) was specifically developed to provide a simple and reliable estimate of malignancy risk in this clinical setting. This study aimed to externally validate the LIONS PREY model and to compare its predictive performance with the Brock and Herder models in patients undergoing index navigational bronchoscopy for pulmonary lesion evaluation. METHODS: We retrospectively analysed patients who underwent index navigational bronchoscopy for peripheral pulmonary lesions between December 2019 and March 2024 at a tertiary academic centre. Malignancy risk was estimated using the LIONS PREY, Brock, and Herder models. Model performance was assessed via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and classification accuracy. RESULTS: Among 193 evaluable lesions, 134 (69.4%) were histologically confirmed malignant. Malignant lesions were associated with increased growth dynamics (2.7 ± 4.1 mm vs. 1.0 ± 4.3 mm, p < 0.001) and spiculation (56.0% vs. 23.7%, p < 0.001). The LIONS PREY achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.94, outperforming Herder (AUC 0.72; p < 0.001) and Brock (AUC 0.62; p < 0.001) models. Correct classification rates were highest for LIONS PREY (85.0%) versus Herder (70.3%) and Brock (69.1%) (all p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: The LIONS PREY demonstrated superior predictive accuracy over Brock and Herder in high-risk patients undergoing navigational bronchoscopy, supporting its clinical utility for malignancy risk stratification.

papers.authors: Barton EC, Warren FC, Zheng S, Symonds J, Tucker E, Jackson K, Pearce C, Fahy M et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: University of Bristol Academic Respiratory Unit, Southmead Hospital, Bristol, UK.
papers.results: 中位住院时间8天（IQR 4-21天）；中位自发缓解时间3天（IQR 1-9天）；全因6个月死亡率22%（n=46）。住院时间延长相关因素：衰弱程度增加（sHR 0.29，95%CI 0.20-0.42）、近期加重（sHR 0.66，95%CI 0.47-0.92）、接受干预（sHR 0.34，95%CI 0.22-0.55）。自发缓解时间延长相关因素：大号肋间胸管（HR 0.57，95%CI 0.32-0.99）、近期加重（HR 0.61，95%CI 0.8-0.97）。衰弱程度增加与6个月死亡率升高相关（OR 10.89，95%CI 4.03-29.42）。
papers.authors_conclusion: 这是迄今最大的前瞻性SSP队列研究；这些数据描述了SSP人群及住院时间、持续性漏气和死亡率的预测因素；衰弱与更差结局相关；近期加重和大号胸管与持续性漏气风险增加相关；保守管理被常用，且在多数病例中成功。

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Evidence guiding management and prognostication of secondary spontaneous pneumothorax (SSP) is scarce. We describe characteristics and outcomes of SSP patients in a prospective UK cohort. METHODS: This is a multicentre, prospective, observational cohort study of patients presenting with SSP to 21 UK hospitals over 6 months. Predictors of time to discharge, time to spontaneous resolution and 6-month mortality were analysed using competing risks survival analysis, Cox and logistic regression. RESULTS: Of 213 recruited patients, 138 (65%) were male; median age was 68 years. 155 (73%) underwent immediate pleural intervention; 58 (27%) received initial conservative management, of whom four subsequently underwent intervention. Median time to discharge was 8 days (IQR 4-21 days). Median time to spontaneous resolution was 3 days (IQR 1-9 days). All-cause 6-month mortality was 22% (n=46). Longer time to discharge was associated with increasing frailty (subhazard ratio (sHR) 0.29, 95% CI 0.20-0.42), recent exacerbation (sHR 0.66, 95% CI 0.47-0.92) and intervention (0.34, 95% CI 0.22-0.55). Large intercostal chest drains (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.32-0.99) and recent exacerbation (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.8-0.97) were associated with longer time to spontaneous resolution. Increasing frailty was associated with increased 6-month mortality (OR 10.89, 95% CI 4.03-29.42). DISCUSSION: This represents the largest prospective SSP cohort study to date. These data describe the SSP population and predictors of time to discharge, persistent air leak and mortality. Frailty was associated with poorer outcomes. Recent exacerbation and larger bore chest drain were associated with increased risk of persistent air leak. Conservative management was commonly used, successfully in most cases.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Lung-related mortality accounts for up to 20% of total deaths worldwide. Recent studies suggest that six sphingolipid species are associated with decreased lung function and increased risk of COPD. We hypothesised that these sphingolipids are associated with increased risk of lung-related mortality. METHODS: Sphingolipid and mortality data were obtained from 4612 participants in the Cardiovascular Health Study, a prospective cohort of older adults (mean age 77 years). Ceramides (Cer-14, Cer-16, Cer-18) and sphingomyelins (SM-14, SM-16, SM-18) were measured in plasma. Multivariable Cox regression was used to examine associations of sphingolipids with three primary outcomes: chronic respiratory, lung cancer and pneumonia mortality. RESULTS: After a median follow-up of 10.2 years, 4099 total deaths had occurred, including 207 chronic respiratory deaths, 171 lung cancer deaths and 210 pneumonia deaths. Of the six sphingolipids examined in this report, four (Cer-16, Cer-18, SM-16 and SM-18) were significantly associated with chronic respiratory mortality and lung cancer mortality; no significant associations were seen with death due to pneumonia. For every 2-fold increase in each of these four sphingolipid species, the association with chronic respiratory mortality and lung cancer mortality ranged from 50% to over 400% higher. When examining 153 COPD-related deaths, a subset of the 207 chronic respiratory deaths, the associations with these four sphingolipids strengthened. CONCLUSION: Cer-16, Cer-18, SM-16 and SM-18 are associated with a higher risk of both chronic respiratory mortality and lung cancer mortality but not pneumonia mortality. Further studies are needed to better understand the mechanistic role of sphingolipids in lung-related mortality.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The prevalence of Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) pulmonary disease shows a sustained upward trend, with treatment challenged by intrinsic drug resistance and toxicity of conventional therapies. Aminoglycosides (AG) are key agents for MAC management, but injectable AGs exhibit poor pulmonary targeting and severe systemic toxicity, particularly ototoxicity. Inhaled AG formulations enhance local lung delivery and reduce systemic exposure. This network meta-analysis (NMA) compared efficacy and safety of inhaled versus injectable AG regimens for microbiologically verified MAC pulmonary disease. METHODS: PubMed, CNKI, and Wanfang databases were searched from inception to January 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and cohort studies. The primary endpoint was 6-month sustained sputum culture conversion; secondary endpoints included ototoxicity, nephrotoxicity, and respiratory adverse events. Bias risk and evidence quality were assessed via RoB 2.0/ROBINS-I and GRADE, respectively. A frequentist fixed-effect network meta-analysis (NMA) was conducted (PROSPERO: CRD420251159363). RESULTS: Four studies (three RCTs and one cohort study, total n = 517) were included, with no statistical heterogeneity (I² = 0%). Inhaled aminoglycosides significantly improved 6-month sustained sputum culture conversion compared with standard therapy (OR = 4.27, 95% CI: 2.38-7.66; moderate-quality evidence per GRADE). Injectable aminoglycosides showed no significant benefit (OR = 1.88, 95% CI: 0.37-9.54; very low-quality evidence). No ototoxicity or nephrotoxicity was observed with inhaled aminoglycosides in the three RCTs (0/302), whereas the injectable aminoglycoside group (single cohort, n = 19) reported a 78.9% ototoxicity rate. Inhaled regimens ranked highest by P-score (0.912). This review is limited by a small total study count (n = 4), reliance on a single observational cohort for injectable regimens, lack of direct head-to-head trials, and imprecision in indirect comparisons. CONCLUSIONS: Inhaled aminoglycoside regimens appear to yield greater efficacy and a more favorable safety profile than standard therapy, particularly in patients with nodular/bronchiectatic phenotype. Injectable regimens may be considered as salvage therapy for severe fibrocavitary cases due to limited high-quality evidence and substantial toxicity. Further head-to-head RCTs are warranted.

papers.abstract_en: AIM: To compare the effects of telerehabilitation-based individual and group exercise, against routine treatment on exercise capacity, lung function, muscle strength, anaerobic power, balance, quality of life (QoL), and change in clinical status in people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF). METHODS: Forty-five pwCF (8-18 years) were randomly allocated into three groups: (1) telerehabilitation-based group or (2) telerehabilitation-based individual exercise, and (3) control arm. Telerehabilitation-based groups underwent supervised exercise programmes 3 days/week via an online platform, and the control arm continued their routine care during an 8-week period. Exercise capacity of PwCF was assessed with 6-min walk test and incremental shuttle walk test. Spirometry measurements, muscle, and handgrip strength were recorded and evaluated. Anaerobic power via vertical jump test, balance via TimedUp and GoTest, and quality of life via Pediatric QoL Inventory were assessed as well. Adherence rates to exercise programmes were calculated. Change in clinical status for all groups, and motivation and enjoyment in the intervention groups were assessed. RESULTS: Forty-one participants completed the study. Both exercise groups showed greater improvements than the control group in the 6-min walk distance, incremental shuttle walk test distance, the Timed Up and Go test, vertical jump performance, participant-reported QoL, and most upper- and lower-extremity muscle strength outcomes (all p < 0.05), with no significant differences between the two exercise groups. Significant group × time interactions were also observed for FEV1 and FEV1/FVC. Handgrip strength and parent-reported QoL did not differ between groups. CONCLUSION: The current study demonstrates similar effects between tele-exercise sessions, with better outcomes than control group. Clinical teams can integrate telerehabilitation-based group exercise into CF centres. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: NCT05590169.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung transplantation (LTx) is a therapeutic option for people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) with end-stage lung disease, however national data on long-term outcomes remain limited. CFTR-modulators have changed the disease course, making pre-modulator era data essential as a benchmark. This study evaluated survival, cumulative incidence of CLAD and clinical outcomes after LTx in Belgium. METHODS: A nationwide retrospective study included all pwCF from the Belgian Cystic Fibrosis Registry who underwent LTx, between 1998 and 2020, with follow-up until December 2020. Kaplan-Meier analyses assessed patient, graft, and post-CLAD survival. The cumulative incidence of CLAD was estimated using Gray's method, accounting for competing risks. Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray models evaluated covariate effects. RESULTS: In total 262 recipients (45% male, median age at LTx 28.4 years) were included. Five- and 10- year survival rates reached 83% and 74%. Recipient age at Tx increased over time. The cumulative incidence of CLAD at 5 and 10 years was 24% and 39%. In descriptive multivariable analyses, more recent Tx year was associated with improved recipient survival and a lower cumulative incidence of CLAD whereas Tx year was not associated with survival after CLAD onset. Among survivors, insulin use increased from 37% pre-LTx to 56% at 5 years post-Tx, while underweight prevalence decreased. CONCLUSIONS: In CF LTx recipients, long-term survival was favorable and more recent Tx year was associated with improved recipient survival and lower cumulative incidence of CLAD. However, survival after CLAD onset did not change significantly over the Tx years.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: We examined the prevalence of mild sleep apnea syndrome (SAS) among Japanese workers, its associations with glucose intolerance and work productivity, and how well conventional screening parameters identify it. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study at a medical foundation hospital in Tokyo, Japan (December 2023-February 2024), 71 employees (17 men, 54 women) underwent home sleep apnea testing to derive the respiratory event index (REI). We also used annual health checkup data, the Japanese Epworth Sleepiness Scale (JESS), the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI-J), and the WHO Health and Work Performance Questionnaire. Glucose intolerance was defined by fasting glucose ≥110 mg/dL, HbA1c ≥6.0%, or current treatment. Multivariable logistic regression (REI≥5 with BMI) and six-variable linear regression (age, sex, BMI, REI≥5, PSQI-J, JESS) were applied. RESULTS: REI≥5 was found in 49.3% of participants. It was associated with glucose intolerance (crude OR 7.6, 95%CI 1.5-37.3, p=0.006), and the link held after adjusting for BMI (adjusted OR 5.49, 1.02-29.57, p=0.047). REI did not correlate with JESS (r=-0.046). For identifying REI≥5, the area under the ROC curve (95%CI) was 0.419 (0.285-0.552) for JESS, 0.737 (0.619-0.855) for BMI, and 0.769 (0.660-0.877) for age. In the regression for absolute presenteeism (model F p=0.005), REI≥5 (β=-0.298, p=0.036) and PSQI-J (β=-0.264, p=0.027) were independent predictors. JESS predicted absenteeism (β=0.250, p=0.040). CONCLUSIONS: Mild or greater SAS was associated with glucose intolerance and with lower presenteeism, whereas sleepiness- and obesity-based indices discriminated poorly. These cross-sectional findings suggest that objective sleep testing merits prospective evaluation as an adjunct to workplace health checkups.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis (HP) is an interstitial lung disease that may present as fibrotic (fHP) or non-fibrotic (nfHP). Fibrosis is associated with progression and poor outcomes; however, the transition to progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) and its predictors remain unclear. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed adult patients diagnosed with HP at a tertiary hospital (2010 and 2022). Patients were classified as having fHP or nfHP and were followed up for at least 1 year. Clinical, functional, radiological, and histological variables were analyzed. PPF was defined according to the 2022 clinical practice guideline of the American Thoracic Society (ATS), European Respiratory Society (ERS), Japanese Respiratory Society (JRS), and Asociación Latinoamericana de Tórax (ALAT). RESULTS: Of 298 HP patients, 191 were included (153 fHP and 38 nfHP). Among patients with fHP, 76 (49.7%) developed PPF after a median of 3.2 years. Median survival was 4.8 years in fHP with PPF versus 6.3 years without, with 1.6 years from PPF onset to death or transplantation. The independent predictors of PPF and survival were lower forced vital capacity, elevated lactate dehydrogenase, fibroblastic foci, and microscopic honeycombing. CONCLUSION: Nearly half of fHP patients progressed to PPF within a few years, with markedly reduced survival. Early recognition of high-risk patients may support timely antifibrotic treatment and improve outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Right atrial (RA) remodeling is closely related to disease severity and outcomes in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), but the prognostic value of coupling RA structure with mechanical performance remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the clinical correlates, reproducibility, prognostic value, and incremental prognostic information of a three-dimensional right atrial coupling index (RACI) in PAH. METHODS: In this single-center bidirectional cohort, 158 treatment-naïve patients with PAH underwent right heart catheterization and echocardiography. RACI was calculated as the three-dimensional right atrial volume index divided by tissue Doppler a' velocity. The primary outcome was all-cause death or hospitalization for worsening right heart failure. Prognostic associations were assessed using multivariable Cox regression, Kaplan-Meier analysis, time-dependent ROC analysis, nested models, and bootstrap internal validation. RESULTS: During follow-up, 27 patients died and 36 were hospitalized for right heart failure. Each 2-unit increase in RACI was independently associated with the composite outcome (HR 1.21, 95% CI 1.04-1.41; P = 0.016), while the cohort-derived cutoff of 3.84 was associated with higher risk (HR 4.09, 95% CI 1.95-8.58; P < 0.001). Higher RACI correlated with larger RA size, higher mRAP/NT-proBNP, and worse RV function. Adding RACI to COMPERA 2.0 and mRAP yielded only a modest increase in C-index (ΔC=0.011, 95% CI -0.008-0.052; P = 0.456), although model fit improved. Intra- and interobserver ICCs were 0.98 and 0.96, respectively. CONCLUSION: RACI was reproducible and independently associated with adverse outcomes in PAH, providing complementary prognostic information that requires prospective multicenter validation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung cancer (LC) remains a global health concern, requiring updates on patterns over time. This study evaluated the burden of LC in Kazakhstan, where data are notably sparse. METHODS: Using the National Cancer Registry data from 2014 to 2023, we evaluated age-standardized incidence, all-cause mortality, and prevalence rates, as well as rates for early-stage LC detection, and calculated the average annual percent change (AAPC) for all measures. We employed restricted mean survival time (RMST) models to evaluate the impact of clinical and demographic factors on survival during the one month through the fifth year following LC diagnosis. We also benchmarked our estimates against the Global Burden Study (GBD). FINDINGS: This study included 39,071 patients. The AAPC for incidence, mortality, and prevalence rates were -2.27% (95% CI, -3.28% to -1.23%), 3.51% (95% CI, -0.76% to 7.97%), and 12.69% (95% CI, 7.53%-18.09%), respectively. LC was diagnosed at advanced stages, with 73.09% classified as stage III and IV, with an AAPC for early-stage detection rates of 0.27% (95% CI, -0.81% to 1.31%). The median follow-up time was 1930 days (reverse Kaplan-Meier method). The 1 month and 5-year survival rates were 83.79% and 20.20%, respectively. The RMST identified that survival was primarily affected by the late stage and older age, where the difference in survival time increased from 1 day at baseline to several years by the fifth year post-diagnosis. INTERPRETATION: Our estimates reflect the escalating public health challenges in Kazakhstan. LC is primarily diagnosed in advanced stages, making preventive measures particularly important. FUNDING: This study was funded by the Committee of Science of the Ministry of Science and Higher Education of the Republic of Kazakhstan (grant number BR24992950, "Creation and Implementation of Innovative Treatment Methods for Oncological Diseases").

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Endoscopic lung volume reduction (ELVR) via valves is a proven therapeutic option for patients with advanced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and emphysema without collateral ventilation. Body mass index (BMI), a simple measure of adiposity, has a complex relationship with COPD. A lower BMI is associated with increased mortality in this patient population. However, the influence of BMI on the outcome of ELVR remains unclear. METHODS: This analysis was conducted with data from the Lung Emphysema Registry (www.lungenemphysemregister.de), a national, prospective, multicentric, producer-independent, open-label clinical trial. The aim of this study was to evaluate the impact of baseline BMI on treatment outcomes after ELVR. Patients were grouped according to their BMI as follows: underweight (BMI <20 kg/m2, n = 76), normal weight (20-24.9 kg/m2, n = 282), overweight (BMI = 25-30 kg/m2, n = 146), and obese (BMI >30 kg/m2, n = 45). RESULTS: Baseline parameters were characteristic of patients with advanced lung emphysema. Emphysema scores and heterogeneity indices of the target lobe were greater in patients with lower BMI. Patients with a lower BMI had worse lung function parameters (FEV1, RV, DLCO, pCO2) and a higher CAT score. All groups showed significant improvements after ELVR at the 3-month follow-up in terms of lung function parameters, exercise capacity, and quality of life. Treatment outcomes were comparable across BMI groups, with the notable exception of more pronounced improvement in CAT scores among underweight patients. The complication rates were low and comparable among the groups, although obese patients had a higher rate of ICU admissions. CONCLUSION: This study suggests that ELVR provides meaningful clinical benefits regardless of BMI in patients with advanced lung emphysema, particularly when dyspnea is primarily attributable to pulmonary pathology. The findings suggest that BMI should be considered as a reflection of disease phenotype and clinical state rather than serving as a predictor for treatment response after ELVR.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To determine whether PaO2/FiO2-based dynamic treatment strategies can optimise the timing of switching from controlled to assisted ventilation. DESIGN AND SETTING: Target trial emulation using the MIMIC-IV database v3.1 (2008-2022). PATIENTS: Adult ICU patients on controlled invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) for ≥ 48 h with at least one PaO2/FiO2 <300 mmHg. A sensitivity analysis included patients ventilated for ≥ 24 h, excluding post-surgical patients. INTERVENTIONS: We compared strategies defined by switching once PaO2/FiO2 exceeded predefined thresholds (150, 200, or 250 mmHg). Additionally, to account for possible PEEP-dependent effects, the thresholds were evaluated depending on the set PEEP (< 8 vs. ≥8 cmH2O), yielding nine strategies. Outcomes were 28-day restricted mean time lost (RMTL) to successful extubation (where a lower RMTL indicates a longer time to extubation) and mortality. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Among 1,635 patients, the strategy of delaying the switch until PaO2/FiO2 >250 mmHg showed a longer time to successful extubation compared to switching at > 150 mmHg or > 200 mmHg (RMTL 17.4 days [95% CI: 15.9-18.6] vs. 19.6 days [95% CI: 18.6-20.9] and 19.8 days [95% CI: 18.5-21.1], respectively). Exploratory PEEP-dependent analyses demonstrated the longest time to successful extubation with '>250 mmHg' for both low and high PEEP and the shortest with '>150 mmHg for low PEEP; >200 mmHg for high PEEP'. Among patients ventilated for ≥ 24 h, the 150 mmHg threshold was most favourable, irrespective of PEEP. No mortality differences were observed across strategies. CONCLUSIONS: Switching as soon as PaO2/FiO2 >150 mmHg is generally favoured over delaying until > 250 mmHg. Patients requiring ≥ 48 h of controlled IMV with PEEP ≥ 8 cmH2O may potentially benefit from a slightly higher threshold (> 200 mmHg). Prospective validation is warranted.

papers.abstract_en: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) causes acute lower respiratory infections, primarily affecting young children and older adults, with seasonal outbreaks peaking annually in March or April in the United States and other temperate regions in the Northern hemisphere. However, the factors driving HMPV seasonality in the United States remain poorly understood. We analyzed laboratory-confirmed HMPV cases and age-specific emergency department visits across 10 US regions, fitting an age-stratified dynamic transmission model to assess spatiotemporal patterns and investigate the influence of environmental variables and viral interference from RSV on HMPV transmission rates. We found that models incorporating climate variables into the transmission rate, including vapor pressure, precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, and minimum temperature, could not capture the timing of HMPV activity across all regions. Instead, HMPV timing was associated with RSV activity, with the HMPV transmission rate reduced in the presence of RSV. We showed that among the candidate models considered, only the models that included an RSV-associated term could reproduce the biennial pattern of HMPV observed in some regions, characterized by alternating "late-small" and "early-large" epidemics. When the best-fit model including the RSV-associated term was used to predict the potential impact of RSV interventions on HMPV transmission, we found that RSV interventions are unlikely to result in a substantial increase in HMPV activity despite reducing competition from RSV. Our work unravels the spatiotemporal dynamics of HMPV and its interaction with RSV, informing future seasonal forecasting and intervention strategies for HMPV.

papers.abstract_en: To develop an interpretable contrast-enhanced CT-based framework for benign-malignant lung tumor classification by integrating radiology-style semantic representations with global pulmonary vascular morphology features. Two particular difficulties with this task lie in (1) establishing an interpretable model to distinguish tumor data that are difficult to differentiate between benign and malignant in clinical practice, and (2) based on clinical experience, incorporate the vascular characteristics around the tumor into the decision-making process. We propose a vascular knowledge-enhanced classification framework that integrates semantic tumor representations extracted by large multimodal models with peritumoral vascular morphological features. The framework consists of three components: (1) an interpretable feature extractor for tumor representation learning, (2) vascular morphology modeling derived from vessel segmentation, and (3) a feature fusion module combining tumor and vascular information for classification. In a retrospective cohort of 420 patients with pathologically confirmed pulmonary tumors, the proposed method was assessed using patient-level, stratified five-fold cross-validation. Relative to the semantic-only branch, decision-level fusion increased accuracy (71.4% vs. 75.5%), AUC (0.764 vs. 0.816), and specificity (57.3% vs. 77.8%), but decreased sensitivity (81.1% vs. 73.9%). These findings indicate that vascular prior-guided correction primarily enhanced benign-case recognition and suppressed false-positive malignant predictions, at the expense of sensitivity for malignant cases. In single-center validation, pulmonary vascular morphology offered complementary structural evidence for differentiating benign from malignant pulmonary tumors larger than 3 cm. The proposed AND-like decision-level correction rule enhanced specificity by reducing false-positive malignant predictions.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: LUAD adopts heterogeneous oncogenic signalling states, and bias toward a PI3K-AKT-mTOR-engaged state is not fully explained by canonical pathway lesions. Because membrane-proximal spatial organization can tune receptor-proximal signalling yet is difficult to quantify in human tumours, we used cilia-associated epithelial programs as a hypothesis-generating entry point to identify convergently perturbed candidates and evaluate their relationship with PI3K engagement. METHODS: We performed intersection-based multi-omic prioritization in TCGA-LUAD, evaluated dependency directionality using DepMap/CCLE expression with CRISPR dependency profiles, and tested the functional relationship between ERICH3 loss and PI3K engagement by siRNA perturbation with PI3K-inhibitor rescue. We anchored tumour context using bulk co-expression, spatial transcriptomics, and single-cell analyses with ERICH3 stratified by transcript "detection", complemented by CellChat-based communication inference and structure/variant-informed hypothesis nomination. RESULTS: ERICH3 was prioritized through a cilia-informed screen as a convergently attenuated candidate, showed reduced protein in paired LUAD specimens (16/24, 66.7%; P = 0.014), promoter hypermethylation, and favourable survival association. An external DepMap dependency screen nominated PI3K-AKT-mTOR dependency directionality in ERICH3-low contexts (Hallmark NES = - 1.79; P = 1.04 × 10⁻4), which was subsequently evaluated functionally in LUAD cell lines. In LUAD cell lines, ERICH3 knockdown increased PI3K-AKT-mTOR phosphorylation and malignant phenotypes, which were attenuated by PI3K inhibition, supporting a functional relationship between ERICH3 loss and PI3K pathway engagement. Multi-scale transcriptomic analyses showed that ERICH3 transcripts were detected predominantly in a mucous epithelial compartment and non-tumour epithelium; CellChat suggested hypothesis-generating immune-interaction signals associated with ERICH3-detected mucous cells. Structural modelling and tumour-variant mapping nominated discrete membrane-proximal regions for mechanism-discriminating follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings support a testable model in which attenuation of ERICH3, identified through a cilia-informed epithelial framework, is associated with a PI3K-engaged malignant state in LUAD. The present study does not establish that ERICH3 directly regulates primary-cilium formation, ciliary protein localization, or ligand-induced ciliary signalling; the precise upstream membrane-proximal and/or cilia-related route remains to be defined.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a highly prevalent and lethal malignancy worldwide. Its pronounced heterogeneity and limited therapeutic options present substantial clinical challenges. Mitochondria and programmed cell death (PCD) markedly regulate tumor development, but their precise roles in LUAD pathogenesis remain unclear. This study aims to identify key genes associated with mitochondrial function and PCD, construct a prognostic model for LUAD, and investigate the prognostic significance and potential protumorigenic mechanisms of VDAC1 in this context. METHODS: We integrated single‑cell RNA‑seq (GSE131907) with bulk transcriptomic data from TCGA‑LUAD and GEO. A LASSO‑Cox regression‑based prognostic signature was built and validated. Single‑cell subclustering, pseudotime trajectory, and cell-cell communication analyses were performed to dissect VDAC1's cell‑type‑specific roles. In vitro functional assays (CCK‑8, colony formation, Transwell, flow cytometry, Western blot) and rescue experiments with the ROS scavenger NAC were conducted in A549 and H1975 cells. Co‑immunoprecipitation was used to examine the VDAC1-AKT interaction. RESULTS: A five‑gene prognostic signature (ACSL1, VDAC1, CYCS, GLS2, MPV17L) was established and validated, effectively stratifying patients into high‑ and low‑risk groups with distinct survival outcomes. Single‑cell resolution revealed that VDAC1 is highly enriched in malignant epithelial cells, inflammatory cancer‑associated fibroblasts, and immunosuppressive M2 macrophages, where it drives proliferation, extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, and lipid metabolic reprogramming, respectively. VDAC1 was markedly overexpressed in LUAD tissues and cell lines; high VDAC1 expression independently correlated with advanced TNM stage, lymph node metastasis, and poor prognosis. VDAC1 knockdown suppressed proliferation, migration, invasion, and EMT, induced G0/G1 arrest and apoptosis, decreased ATP production and oxygen consumption rates, and increased ROS levels. Mechanistically, VDAC1 activated the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway and directly interacted with AKT (co‑immunoprecipitation). NAC‑mediated ROS scavenging only partially rescued the si‑VDAC1‑induced suppression of signaling, EMT, and proliferation, indicating a ROS‑dependent mechanism complemented by a ROS‑independent direct interaction. Additionally, VDAC1 expression was negatively correlated with most antitumor immune cells and positively associated with immune checkpoint molecules (e.g., PD‑L1), suggesting an immunosuppressive microenvironment. CONCLUSIONS: We present a novel mitochondria‑ and PCD‑related five‑gene prognostic model for LUAD. VDAC1 is identified as a key oncogenic driver that promotes LUAD progression through dual mechanisms: ROS‑mediated activation of PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling and direct physical interaction with AKT, leading to EMT, metabolic reprogramming, and immunosuppressive microenvironment remodeling. These findings establish that VDAC1 is a promising prognostic biomarker and a potential therapeutic target in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis (TB) treatment outcomes are influenced not only by disease-specific programs but also by broader health system capacity and population-level vulnerabilities. This study examined the determinants of TB treatment success in low- and lower-middle-income countries and assessed whether these associations differed across income groups. METHODS: An unbalanced country-year panel dataset comprising 1,216 observations from 56 low- and lower-middle-income countries between 2001 and 2023 was analyzed. The dependent variable was the treatment success rate among new TB cases. The independent variables included infectious disease service coverage, TB case detection rate, TB incidence, health expenditure, out-of-pocket health expenditure, immunization coverage, undernutrition, HIV prevalence, malaria incidence, population growth, and life expectancy. Associations were estimated using a two-way fixed-effects model with Driscoll-Kraay robust standard errors. Robustness checks and income-group subgroup analyses were also conducted. RESULTS: Infectious disease service coverage (β = 0.0925; p = 0.003), immunization coverage (β = 0.0845; p = 0.002), population growth (β = 0.9145; p = 0.012), and life expectancy (β = 0.3911; p = 0.001) were positively associated with TB treatment success. Per capita health expenditure showed a positive but marginally significant association (β = 1.4590; p = 0.053). Undernutrition was also positively associated with treatment success (β = 0.2911; p < 0.001); however, this unexpected ecological finding should not be interpreted as evidence of a protective effect. In low-income countries, infectious disease service coverage and TB case detection were positively associated with treatment success, whereas HIV prevalence was negatively associated with it. In lower-middle-income countries, health expenditure, immunization coverage, undernutrition, population growth, and life expectancy showed positive associations. CONCLUSION: TB treatment success is associated with broader health system conditions, although its determinants vary across income groups. Strengthening infectious disease service coverage, case detection, TB-HIV service integration, routine preventive health services, and the effective use of health resources may contribute to improved treatment outcomes. The unexpected macro-level association observed for undernutrition warrants further investigation using multilevel and patient-level data.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The incidence of lung cancer in women is increasing, yet the effect of smoking history on survival remains uncertain. METHODS: Adults who underwent resection for non-small cell lung cancer (2015-2024), from the Society of Thoracic Surgeons database, were grouped by sex and smoking status. Outcomes were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression and Cox models. RESULTS: In total, 145,103 patients were identified (current or former smoker women: 65,650 [45.2%]; current or former smoker men: 55,912 [38.5%]; never-smoker women: 16,902 [11.7%]; never-smoker men: 6,639 [4.6%]. Median age was 69 years. Never-smoker women were more likely to be Asian, have clinical stage I disease, and have adenocarcinoma; they also had the lowest rates of 30-day mortality and major morbidity. Current or former smoker men had the highest complications rates. These findings persisted after risk adjustment. Longitudinal mortality data were available for 59,756 patients (57%). Five-year survival was 79% for never-smoker women, 70% for never-smoker men, 71% for current or former smoker women, and 58% for current or former smoker men. Risk-adjusted survival was longer in women versus men and in never-smokers versus current or former smokers for both sexes. Compared with never-smoker women, all-cause mortality risk was higher in current or former smoker women (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]=1.18 [95% confidence interval {CI},1.11-1.26]), never-smoker men (aHR=1.44[95% CI,1.30-1.60]), and current or former smoker men (aHR=1.71 [95% CI,1.59-1.84]). CONCLUSIONS: Never-smoker women had the lowest perioperative risk and superior long-term survival, highlighting sex and smoking status as independent determinants of outcomes after lung cancer resection.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: High blood eosinophil counts can predict an enhanced response to inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), but additional insight in treatment effect heterogeneity is needed to optimize clinical disease management. We investigated if causal machine learning models can detect heterogeneity in the effect of two ICS-containing therapies on both time to first exacerbation and exacerbation rate, and if this approach can identify additional predictors of ICS response. METHODS: Baseline characteristics from patients in the fluticasone furoate/umeclidinium/vilanterol (FF/U/V) and U/V arms of the InforMing the PAthway of COPD Treatment (IMPACT) trial (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT02164513) were used to train a causal survival forest to estimate the effect of fluticasone furoate (an ICS) on time to first exacerbation for each patient. Similarly, a causal forest was trained for exacerbation rate. Results were averaged over 100 train and validation sets in a Monte-Carlo cross-validation approach. The analysis was repeated for a comparison of the FF/V and U/V arms. RESULTS: This analysis included 4048 FF/U/V, 4034 FF/V and 2025 U/V patients. Significant p-values for AUTOC (area under the targeting operator characteristic) curve indicated that all models ranked patients well according to individualized treatment and that significant heterogeneity was detected in the effect of ICS on both exacerbation outcomes. Respiratory symptoms, reversibility of airflow limitation and lung function, in addition to eosinophils, were identified as important predictors by all models. The contribution of additional predictors in determining the effect of ICS was most apparent for patients at the lower end of the eosinophil spectrum. CONCLUSIONS: This hypothesis-generating secondary analysis of IMPACT detected significant heterogeneity in the effect of ICS and indicated that, in addition to eosinophils, other clinical patient characteristics also contribute to the prediction of ICS response on both time to first exacerbation and exacerbation rate. The causal machine learning approach in this analysis can identify treatment effect predictors and patterns of response, to enhance insight in COPD disease phenotypes and heterogeneous treatment effects.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The efficacy of consolidation immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) after induction chemoimmunotherapy (iCIT) followed by definitive chemoradiotherapy (dCRT) in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unclear. We investigated the survival benefit of consolidation ICIs and identified potential beneficiaries. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with locally advanced ESCC who received iCIT followed by dCRT at 11 Chinese institutions between October 2020 and December 2023. Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were compared between consolidation and non-consolidation groups using propensity score matching (PSM), with inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) as a sensitivity analysis. Prognostic factors were evaluated using Cox regression models, and subgroup analyses explored treatment heterogeneity. RESULTS: Among 636 patients, 238 received consolidation ICIs and 398 received none consolidation therapy. After 1:1 PSM, 226 patients remained in each group. Consolidation ICIs significantly improved OS (HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.43-0.83; P = 0.002) and PFS (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.55-0.94; P = 0.016). These findings were consistent with IPTW and multivariable analysis. In exploratory analyses, patients with stable disease after iCIT showed a trend toward greater benefit from consolidation ICIs. Consolidation ICIs were associated with reduced multiple distant metastasis (0.44% vs 5.75%, P = 0.002). CONCLUSION: In this retrospective real-world study, consolidation ICIs after iCIT followed by dCRT were associated with improved survival in locally advanced ESCC, with a numerically greater benefit in patients achieving stable disease after induction therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary artery (PA) reconstruction permits parenchyma-sparing resection in selected central lung cancers; its robotic application, however, requires control of a fragile vessel in a confined operative field. This narrative review examines published robot-assisted PA reconstruction, procedural configurations, haemorrhage management, patient selection and relevant video-assisted thoracoscopic (VATS) and open evidence. PubMed/MEDLINE and publisher sources were searched through 26 October 2026, with priority given to studies identifying actual PA repairs separately from bronchial sleeve operations. The early 30-patient uniportal robotic sleeve series contained four PA reconstructions, whereas a subsequent 134-patient sleeve cohort reported excellent overall margins without a separately extractable PA-specific denominator. In a contemporary series of 49 PA reconstructions after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, 21 operations were open and 28 were reported jointly as VATS/RATS. Small robotic technical series demonstrate tangential repair, angioplasty and circumferential anastomosis, but do not establish comparative vascular safety or durable patency. A large registry found fewer overall conversions during robotic than VATS lobectomy, although robotic conversions were proportionally more often emergent or vascular. Robot-specific safety depends on preplanned proximal and distal occlusion, unobstructed bedside access, disciplined clamp and suture strategies, and immediate conversion capability. Lung autotransplantation remains a separate, highly selected alternative. Available evidence supports feasibility in experienced programmes, not superiority over VATS or thoracotomy. Multicentre, PA-specific reporting is needed to establish vascular outcomes and reproducibility.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis (TB) continues to be one of the deadliest infectious diseases in Malaysia. This nationwide retrospective ecological study aimed to determine the spatial and temporal patterns of TB with the association of sociodemographic and environmental factors in Malaysia. METHODS: The sociodemographic data of 301,822 TB cases from 2014 to 2023 were collected from the Tuberculosis Information System (TBIS). Environmental data were acquired from the Department of Environment Malaysia and the Malaysia Meteorological Department. The Choropleth mapping and heatmapping were used to assess the trend of TB cases, while the Global Moran's I, Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA), and Getis-Ord Gi* were used to assess the spatial pattern of TB cases. Ordinary least squares (OLS) and geographically weighted regression (GWR) models were employed to examine the spatial association between sociodemographic and environmental factors and TB incidence. RESULTS: Global spatial autocorrelation analysis found that the cases were clustered (p < 0.05) over the 10 years, while local spatial autocorrelation detected that the high-high cluster was concentrated in several districts in Selangor and Kuala Lumpur, with in the districts of Klang, Kuala Selangor, Sabak Bernam, Jelebu, Kuala Lumpur, Gombak, Temerloh, Bentong, Sepang, and Hulu Langat. The hotspot districts were consistently in these two states. This could be attributed to the growing rapid urbanization, demographic expansion, migration, and persistent socio-economic differences. Aged 14 years old and younger, aged 65 years old and older, non-Malaysian, Malay, Chinese, Aborigines in Peninsular Malaysia, completed secondary school, completed STPM / diploma / matriculation / foundation, smoking, SO2, and NO2 were associated with TB incidence (p < 0.05). The GWR models identified the spatially varying association in the distribution of TB incidence and its respective combinatory sets of explanatory variables. CONCLUSION: Spatial heterogeneity of TB incidence and persistent hotspot districts throughout Malaysia were explored using spatial analysis. This study emphasizes the importance of integrate spatial data to assist targeted monitoring, surveillance, early case detection, treatment, and the allocation of public health resources in high-burden regions.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) affects 40-60% of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients but remains frequently underdiagnosed and undertreated, contributing to adverse outcomes [1]. METHODS: Our objective was to develop an automated machine learning (ML) classifier to identify potential COPD, and potentially untreated COPD among NSCLC patients. We performed a retrospective cohort study of 4,604 NSCLC patients. Manual chart review (development set; DS; [n = 600]; test set; TS; [n = 294]), using Global Initiative for Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) criteria, served as the reference standard for COPD diagnosis. Predictor selection used least-absolute-shrinkage-and-selection-operator (LASSO) logistic regression. Two logit thresholds were chosen to create binary classifiers: a ≥ 95% specificity quality-improvement threshold (QIT) for COPD identification, and Youden's index threshold (YT) for survival analysis and association with radiographic emphysema. RESULTS: The classifier achieved an area-under-the-receiver-operating-characteristic-curve of 0.93 in the DS and TS (95% CI:0.91-0.95; 95% CI:0.91-0.96, respectively). The QIT yielded logit cutoffs ≥ 0.9242 (DS) and ≥ 0.9625 (TS), with sensitivities 69% and 72%, specificities 95% and 96%, positive-predictive-value (PPV) 93%, and negative-predictive-value (NPV) 77% and 80%, respectively. In the DS and TS, potential COPD prevalence was 48% and 46%, with 41% and 46% potentially untreated; the QIT-classifier identified 69% and 72% of potential COPD cases and 40% and 50% of potentially untreated cases, respectively (PPV 85%, 95% CI:73-93% and 86%, 95% CI:71-95%). YT yielded a sensitivity and specificity of 88%. In Cox-proportional hazards models (n = 4,501, 1,959 deaths), the YT-COPD classifier was associated with increased mortality, with significant effect measure modification by clinical stage (p = 0.003; stratified HR YT-COPD: stage I: 1.71, 95% CI:1.30-2.44, p < 0.001; Stage II: 1.72, 95% CI:1.15-2.59, p = 0.009; Stage III: 1.67, 95% CI:1.34-2.08, p < 0.001; Stage IV: 1.29, 95% CI:1.15-1.44, p < 0.001). Furthermore, classifier-predicted COPD (YT) was strongly associated with radiographic emphysema (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: This ML classifier effectively emulates structured chart review to identify potential COPD and potentially untreated COPD in NSCLC, with prognostic validity and potential for scalable, low-cost quality improvement and research. External validation in other institutions and EHR systems is warranted before broader implementation.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) can lead to severe complications if left untreated. Several challenges hinder OSA identification in females, resulting in underdiagnosis and undertreatment in this population. This study aimed to develop a machine learning (ML) approach specifically tailored to screen women for moderate-to-severe OSA. METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted using clinical records of 1,210 women who underwent polysomnography at our institution. Collected data included demographics, body metrics, nocturnal oxygen saturation levels, medical conditions, medications, laboratory measurements, and polysomnography results. Four ML algorithms were employed to classify participants into moderate-to-severe and none-to-mild OSA groups. RESULTS: Due to the high missingness of laboratory values in the whole cohort, two sets of models were developed: one utilizing all subjects but excluding lab tests, and another restricted to a subgroup of 383 participants that additionally incorporated hemoglobin and lipid profile alongside the other features. Without laboratory measurements, the best-performing model was adaptive boosting, which achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve and accuracy of 0.811 and 76.03%, respectively. When lab tests were included, gradient boosting machine outperformed its competitors, with the above metrics reaching 0.872 and 84.42%, respectively. CONCLUSION: The promising performance of our approach underlines the potential of artificial intelligence in refining screening strategies for OSA in women. Nadir oxygen saturation during sleep emerged as a particularly strong predictor, reinforcing the central role of nocturnal hypoxemia in OSA risk stratification. Future research should focus on incorporating broader clinical inputs and using larger, diverse datasets to develop a highly accurate, robust model that meets clinical standards and is suitable for real-world implementation.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Sex influences asthma phenotypes and treatment outcomes. However, real-world data on sex-related differences in severe asthma patients treated with biologics are limited. The objective of this study was to assess sex differences in baseline characteristics and treatment outcomes in a cohort of severe eosinophilic asthma (SEA) patients treated with biologics. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 370 SEA patients (235 females, 135 males) treated with mepolizumab, benralizumab, or dupilumab. Clinical remission was defined as no OCS use plus at least two of: no exacerbations, ACT ≥20, or FEV1 >80%. Logistic regression was used to identify sex-specific predictors of remission at 24 months. RESULTS: Severe type 2 asthma showed a prevalence in females (female-to-male ratio of 1.7:1). Baseline characteristics revealed higher prevalence of obesity (p = 0.015) and osteoporosis (p = 0.006) in females, and greater tobacco exposure (p = 0.05), FeNO (p = 0.03), and nasal polyposis (p = 0.0002) in males. Males had greater reduction in FeNO (p ≤ 0.05) and more male patients stopped exacerbations at 24 months (p < 0.0001), while females showed greater FEF25-75% (p ≤ 0.05) improvement and larger IgE drops (p < 0.0001). Remission rates were similar across sexes at both 12 months (64.3% versus 74.1%; p = 0.06) and 24 months (71.5% versus 77.0%; p = 0.27). In females, remission was associated with eosinophils >300/μL (OR: 2.68; 95% CI: 1.41-5.07; p = 0.003), FeNO >50 ppb (OR: 21.05; 95% CI: 10.24-43.34; p < 0.0001), and nasal polyposis (OR: 2.74; 95% CI: 1.46-5.13; p = 0.001); obesity (OR: 0.20; 95% CI: 0.11-0.37; p < 0.0001), smoking (OR: 0.38; 95% CI: 0.21-0.70; p = 0.002), anxiety (OR: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.23-0.94; p = 0.04), and reflux (OR: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.27-0.84; p = 0.01) were negative predictors. In males, OCS dependency (OR: 0.35; 95% CI: 0.13-0.94; p = 0.03) and FEV1 <80% (OR: 0.18; 95% CI: 0.05-0.63; p = 0.004) were negative predictors. CONCLUSION: Biologics were equally effective in inducing clinical remission across sexes, but different predictors influenced outcomes. Sex-aware strategies may support personalized asthma care.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Endemic mycoses, caused by Blastomyces, Coccidioides, Emergomyces, Histoplasma, Paracoccidioides, Sporothrix, and Talaromyces marneffei, represent an important global health challenge. Expanding endemic regions, climatic change, improved diagnostics, increased disease awareness, and an increasing at-risk population have contributed to rising case numbers. These infections affect both immunocompetent and immunocompromised hosts and exhibit marked clinical heterogeneity. Current treatment response guidance, established by the Mycoses Study Group and the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer in 2008, are primarily tailored for invasive yeast and mold infections and are inadequate for endemic mycoses due to their complexity and heterogeneity. METHODS: An international, multidisciplinary expert panel convened through the Mycoses Study Group Education and Research Consortium and the European Confederation of Medical Mycology to develop consensus guidance for treatment response assessment in endemic mycoses. The process included a structured literature review, expert discussion, regulatory consultation, patient input, and public comment, culminating in consensus-based response criteria. RESULTS: The proposed guidance response criteria encompass clinical, mycologic, and radiologic assessments. CONCLUSIONS: The new criteria aim to improve the accuracy and standardize the assessment of treatment response, enabling comparison and pooling results across clinical trials while addressing the unique challenges posed by these diverse pathogens.

In this study, we evaluated the safety and feasibility of the new Lung Volume Reduction Reverser (LVR-R) system. METHODS: Prospective, nonrandomized, exploratory, single-center, first-in-man study in 15 patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and severe emphysema. Most affected lung lobes were treated sequentially with the LVR-R coils from May 2019 to JUL 2022. Pulmonary function, 6-min walking distance (6-MWD), questionnaires and adverse events were recorded from baseline to 1-year post-procedure. Computer tomography was acquired at baseline and 6 months. RESULTS: A total of 28 procedures were performed, in which 10 (n = 22, 78.6%), 9 (n = 2, 7.1%), or 8 (n = 4, 14.3%) LVR-R coils were implanted, predominantly in the upper lobes (n = 26/28, 92.86%). Two patients refused a second treatment, one of whom refused follow-ups. Adverse events at 3 months included severe pneumonia and/or COPD exacerbations (n = 7), ventilatory failure (n = 2) and 1 pneumothorax requiring thoracic drainage. Mild hemoptysis occurred in 18 and mild pneumonia and/or COPD exacerbations in 9 patients. Overall, neither FEV1, residual volume, 6-MWD, CAT nor mMRC improved within 1-year (n.s. all). In 2 patients, response in FEV1 >500 mL occurred. CONCLUSION: In this severely diseased and small patient cohort, LVR-R implantation was technically feasible. The complication rate was similar to other coil studies and requires a careful pre-procedure benefit-risk evaluation. Two of fourteen bilaterally treated individuals demonstrated a notable improvement in lung function.
